# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

Systematically inventory the gaps between the current Tech Preview quality of
Llama Stack and the GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope. This resolves
the strategy's open question — the GA scope itself is unknown until this
assessment lands, and the size of the downstream stability and hardening work
is currently only an estimate.

## Scope

- Collect and consolidate TP feedback scattered across support tickets into a
  systematic GA-readiness picture.
- Assess gaps against the GA bar in four enumerated categories:
  - API stability
  - Upgrade paths
  - Scale limits
  - Error handling
- Produce a GA scope document: the definitive, prioritized list of
  GA-blocking gaps and the remediation work they imply, sized so downstream
  stability/hardening work can be planned against it.
- Flag any gap that cannot be absorbed by the planned stability and hardening
  work and warrants additional remediation effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness assessment exists covering all four gap categories (API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) with input from the
  TP support-ticket record.
- Each identified gap is classified as GA-blocking or deferrable, with a
  severity/size estimate.
- The definitive GA scope is published and accepted by stakeholders as the
  authoritative input for GA planning.
- Measured by: downstream GA stability and hardening work can be scoped
  directly from the assessment output without re-deriving the gap inventory.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope.

## Open Questions

- The assessment's outcome determines the final size and shape of the
  stability and hardening work; its result is the gate for that work.

# Llama Stack API stability, upgrade path, and hardening to GA bar

## Description

Establish the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack and close the
stability and hardening gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment, so the
GA distribution meets the quality bar that Tech Preview status currently
excuses.

## Description of dependencies

This work is gated on the GA-readiness assessment: its scope is defined by the
gap inventory that assessment produces. The assessment outcome may resize or
reshape the hardening portion of this work.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution.
- Define and publish a deprecation policy for the API surface.
- Implement and test an upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the GA
  release.
- Remediate the API stability, upgrade path, scale limit, and error handling
  gaps identified as GA-blocking by the GA-readiness assessment.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, with a documented deprecation policy.
- An upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases is tested and passes.
- All GA-blocking gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment within API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling are closed or
  explicitly re-classified with stakeholder sign-off.
- The Konflux build pipeline for Llama Stack remains green.
- Measured by: a user on either of the last two TP releases can upgrade to the
  GA release following documented steps without unsupported manual
  intervention.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases.
- HLR-1 (P0, partial): closes the GA-blocking gaps the readiness assessment
  inventories.

## Risks

- Until the GA-readiness assessment lands, the size of the hardening work is
  an estimate; scope may grow based on its findings.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

Put the production support posture in place that GA requires: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix for Llama
Stack.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the Llama Stack distribution in
  production (e.g., availability and operational objectives appropriate to a
  supported component).
- Define and document a backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for how
  long, and how backports are requested and delivered.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: the distributions,
  providers, and configurations that are supported at GA, and what is
  explicitly unsupported.
- Align the support posture with existing platform support processes and
  escalation paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and agreed with support/product stakeholders.
- The backport policy is documented, covering supported release windows and
  the backport request process.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and distinguishes supported
  from unsupported configurations.
- Measured by: a support engineer answering a production Llama Stack case can
  determine supportability, target SLOs, and backport eligibility from the
  published posture alone.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place — documented SLO targets,
  backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI guardrails integration: supported and documented

## Description

Promote the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration with Llama Stack from an
experimental integration to a supported, documented integration, owned and
validated by the TrustyAI team.

## Description of dependencies

Validation and certification of the integration must run against the
versioned, stability-guaranteed Llama Stack API surface and its tested upgrade
path — a supported integration cannot be certified while that surface is still
in flux.

## Scope

- Validate TrustyAI guardrails (safety provider integration) against the GA
  Llama Stack API surface, including behavior across the tested upgrade path
  from the last two TP releases.
- Define and validate fail-mode behavior when the TrustyAI service is
  unavailable or degraded (consistent with the safety-critical role of
  guardrails).
- Document the integration end to end: supported deployment topologies,
  configuration, capabilities, and limitations, at support-grade quality. This
  epic owns the TrustyAI documentation set for the integration (deployment
  topologies, configuration reference, troubleshooting, support runbooks); the
  Llama Stack GA documentation set covers only the user-facing summary of the
  integration (its default availability in GA distributions and its disable
  path) and is authored by the GA documentation uplift work.
- Establish the TrustyAI-side support posture for the integration (how issues
  are triaged and escalated).
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline for TrustyAI green throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The TrustyAI guardrails integration is validated against the versioned GA
  API surface of Llama Stack, including the tested upgrade path.
- Fail-mode behavior when TrustyAI is unavailable is defined, tested, and
  documented.
- Integration documentation exists at support grade (a support engineer or
  customer can deploy and troubleshoot the integration from it).
- The integration is supported — no longer classified as experimental on the
  TrustyAI side.
- The Konflux build pipeline for TrustyAI remains green.
- Measured by: guardrails deployed per the documentation on a supported
  configuration pass validation, and support can triage issues without
  escalation to engineering for baseline questions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# Enable TrustyAI guardrails by default in Llama Stack GA distributions

## Description

On the Llama Stack distribution side, promote TrustyAI safety guardrails from
an experimental flag to a supported, default-on integration for GA
distributions.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental/opt-in gating for the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration in the Llama Stack distribution so it is a supported
  configuration in GA distributions.
- Make the guardrails integration available by default in GA distributions
  where the TrustyAI service is present.
- Preserve a rollback/disable path so operators can turn the integration off
  per deployment if needed (the flag removal must be reversible).
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green throughout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GA Llama Stack distributions expose TrustyAI guardrails as a supported
  integration without an experimental opt-in flag.
- The integration can be disabled per deployment via a documented rollback
  path.
- The Konflux build pipeline for Llama Stack remains green.
- Measured by: a fresh GA distribution deployment can use TrustyAI guardrails
  without setting any experimental flag or TP opt-in.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

## Risks

- Coordination with the TrustyAI team's support and documentation work on the
  same integration (parallel work in a different repo — coordination risk,
  not a dependency).

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift

## Description

Uplift Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes
from Tech Preview, so the documentation matches the supported, GA product.

## Description of dependencies

Documentation is authored after the implementation work it describes — API
stability guarantees and upgrade path, production support posture, the
supported TrustyAI guardrails integration (including default-on behavior in GA
distributions), and default Dashboard enablement — so it describes what was
actually built.

## Scope

- Uplift existing Llama Stack documentation to GA standards: supported
  configuration guidance, stability and deprecation policy references, and
  support posture (SLOs, backport policy) as user-facing content.
- Write migration notes covering the move from TP releases to GA, including
  the tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.
- Document the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, including its
  default availability in GA distributions and its disable path. This epic owns
